MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  Special City Council Meeting

  July 9, 2019

A Special Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 4:45 p.m., on July 9, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 5, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

PUBLIC COMMENTS

OPEN SESSION

 1.  Casta Del Sol Golf Course

  City Attorney, Bill Curley presented the staff report.

City Council Special Meeting Minutes  1  July 9, 2019
   Thep following expressed support for the City’s purchase of the Casta Del Sol Golf
  Course: Robert Stalter, M.V.; Robert Breton, M.V.; Mike Flynn M.V.; Jim Owens, Lake
  Forest; Rick Sandzimier, M.V.; and Matthew Larsen, M.V.

  The following spoke against the purchase of the Casta Del Sol Golf Course: Gerald
  Voldamino, M.V. and Cathy Schlicht, M.V.

  Gordon Hite, M.V.: stated that the slopes along the golf course pose a fire hazard and
  need to be cleared.

  Dave Tomlinson, M.V.: expressed his concern for future use of the golf course if
  purchased by the City. He stated that he is in favor of a possible park if the golf course
  is not successful.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to
  direct staff to evaluate the City's interests in preserving the Casta Del Sol Public Golf
  Course for public purposes and use, by acquisition of the facility.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  Absent:  None

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 5:42 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this special
session, Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, July 9, 2019, at 5:44 p.m.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of August 27, 2019

City Council Special Meeting Minutes  2  July 9, 2019
   MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 9, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:44 p.m., on July 9, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on July 5, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

PUBLCIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: expressed her dissatisfaction with the way that the City is handling the
potential purchase of the Casta Del Sol Golf Course, as well as the City’s legal representation from
the Law Offices of Lozano Smith.

CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Real Property Negotiator, Government Code Section 54956.8.
  The property commonly referred to as “Casta del Sol Golf Course” located at
  27601 Casta del Sol, Mission Viejo, California. City of Mission Viejo Negotiators:
  City Manager Dennis Wilberg, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public
  Services Keith Rattay, Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas and City

City Council Minutes  1  July 9, 2019
   Attorney William Curley, III. Negotiating Party: Professional Real Estate Services
  (PRES) President Brad Schroth. Under discussion price and terms.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:47 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:20 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council discussed the potential real estate transaction
for the Casta Del Sol Golf Course, but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Wildfire and SCE Reliability

  The City Council received the presentation from Karalee Darnell of SCE Public Affairs.

 P2.  Featured Business of the Month - Custom Comfort Mattress

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamation to Greg Munoz.

 P2B.  Orange County Sheriff Department Resident Recognition

  Sergeant Crowley recognized residents Jeremy, Eric and Eric’s dog Tex for their
  assistance in apprehending a commercial burglary suspect.

 P3.  Connecting People to Services

  The City Council received updates from Quality of Life Deputy Dana
  Chaney, Community Services Supervisor Leslie McDonald, and Carol Sullivan and
  Detrice Young from Mercy House.

 P4.  Proclaim July 2019 To Be National Parks and Recreation Month

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamation to Director of Recreation and Community
  Services Mark Nix and staff.

 P5.  Wildfire Awareness and Prevention Proclamation

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamation to Fire Chief Rob Capobianco.

 P6.  2019 Pacific Symphony and Prelude in the Park Announcement

City Council Minutes  2  July 9, 2019
   The City Council received the presentation from Community Services Manager Lydie
  Gutfeld.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Abdul Rastagar, M.V.: asked that the City Council direct the Orange County Sheriff’s Department
to enforce noise ordinance laws for loud motorcycles and automobiles along Olympiad Parkway.
He suggested posting signs similar to those in Rancho Santa Margarita and Aliso Viejo.

Ronak Naik and Nick Hassas, M.V: thanked the City and the Council for supporting Relay for Life
and they noted that this year’s event raised over $223,000. They announced a new support program
called “Road to Recovery” to facilitate answers to questions that patients or their families may
have regarding cancer treatments. They further thanked City employees Drew Fine, Marcelo
Dario, and Scott Baker, along with the City’s Adopted Marine Battalion for all their help in making
the event possible.

Johnathan Hughes, La Habra: introduced himself as the new Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) Delegate for Orange County.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 12 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of June 25, 2019, as
  presented.

 2.  Check Register dated June 21, 2019 in the amount of $991,440.65

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 3.  Check Register dated June 28, 2019 in the amount of $388,528.91

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for May 2019

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  July 9, 2019
  5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for May 2019

  Received and filed.

 6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for May
  2019

  Received and filed.

 7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly
  Report for May 2019

  Received and filed.

 8.  2019 Residential Resurfacing—Slurry Seal (CIP 20838)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Roy Allan Slurry Seal, Inc.,
  in the amount of $837,774.50.

 9.  Renewed Measure M (M2) Public Works Seven-Year Capital Improvement
  Program

  Adopted Resolution 19-20 Adopting a Renewed Measure M (M2) Seven-Year Public
  Works Capital Improvement Program Beginning with the 2019/2020 Fiscal Year.

 10.  General Plan Amendment GPA2018-32 / Zone Change ZC2018-21 / Planned
  Development Permit PDP2018-303 / Variance VAR2019-51 / and Tentative Tract
  Map TTM18187 - Petitions submitted by Shea Homes Limited Partnership to
  permit residential development on 6.73 acres of the total 10.3-acre Mission Foothill
  shopping center site located at 28715 Los Alisos Boulevard. GPA2018-32 is filed
  to change the subject site’s land use designation from Commercial Highway to
  Residential 30. ZC2018-21 is filed to change the site’s zoning from CH
  (Commercial Highway) and RPD30A (Residential Planned Development,
  Affordable) to RPD30 (Residential Planned Development). The proposed project
  includes demolition of 99,500 square feet of existing retail space to accommodate
  a new 105-dwelling-unit, for-sale project including 44 detached single-family units
  and 61 attached townhome units. All homes would be three stories with an overall
  project density of 15.6 du/ac. Four existing freestanding retail buildings, located
  adjacent to Los Alisos Boulevard, would remain, with the residential development
  occurring to the northeast, between the retail buildings and the SR 241 toll road

  Adopted Ordinance 19-330 Approving Zone Change ZC2018-21, Being a Petition
  Submitted by Shea Homes Limited Partnership to Change the Zoning Map Designation
  from CH (Commercial Highway) and RPD30A (Residential Planned Development,
  Affordable) to RPD30 (Residential Planned Development), for 6.73 Acres of the
  Property Located at 28715 Los Alisos Boulevard, Further Described as a Portion of
  Assessor Parcel Number 839-161-12.

City Council Minutes  4  July 9, 2019
  11.  SCAG Regional Housing Needs Assessment Planning Support Services

  Authorized staff to issue a Purchase Order to GSL Associates in the amount not to
  exceed $50,000 to provide Planning Support Services associated with the Regional
  Housing Needs Assessment.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 12.  Environmental Services (preparation of a Mitigated Negative Declaration)
  required by the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to assess any
  impacts and necessary mitigation associated with the import and storage of dirt
  for future use from the Caltrans widening project along Interstate I-5 to Lower
  Curtis Park Open Space

  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell pointed out that this topic references the import of dirt from
  the Caltrans I-5 widening project for the potential building of future ball parks east of
  Curtis Park.

  Director of Planning and Community Development Elaine Lister stated that the
  proposal is for environmental services required by the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA).

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley to
  authorize staff to enter into an Agreement with Phil Martin & Associates, Inc. in an
  amount not to exceed $58,250, for environmental services (preparation of a Mitigated
  Negative Declaration) required by the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  to assess any impacts and necessary mitigation associated with the import and storage
  of dirt for future use from the Caltrans widening project along Interstate I-5, to Lower
  Curtis Park Open Space.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

 13.  Amending the City of Mission Viejo Salary Schedule and Adopting the Twelfth
  Amendment to City Manager Employment Agreement

  City Attorney, Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  The Council Members praised Dennis Wilberg for his work ethics as City Manager.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley to
  (1) adopt Resolution 19-21 Amending the City’s Salary Schedule Effective August 1,
  2019; and (2) adopt Resolution 19-22 Approving the Twelfth Amendment to the City
  Manager Employment Agreement.
City Council Minutes  5  July 9, 2019
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

 14.  Integrated Solid Waste Management Services

  Environmental Programs Administrator Denise Matson presented the staff report.

  Joe Sloan of Sloan Vasquez McAfee presented a power point presentation and answered
  questions from the Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 19-23 Approving the Second Amendment to the Franchise Agreement
  for Solid Waste Services between the City of Mission Viejo and U.S. Waste of
  California, dba Waste Management of Orange County, and (2) approve the Draft
  Request for Proposals and the Draft Agreement for Integrated Solid Waste Management
  Services with the addition in the Code of Conduct that all communication must be
  conducted through the process established by the Consultant and in conjunction with
  the ad hoc committee and either the City Manager or City Attorney.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

 15.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

 16.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update from Chief Capobianco

  Chief Capobianco presented the report.

 17.  Orange County Sheriff's Department (OCSD) Update from Chief Vuong

  Lt. Vuong presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

City Council Minutes  6  July 9, 2019
   By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum thanked the two members of the public who spoke about Relay for
Life earlier in the meeting. She encouraged people to go to the South Orange County Relay for
Life website and donate if they have not already done so. She announced that throughout the City,
there are many summer concerts: three at Arroyo Trabuco Golf Course and several concerts at
Lake Mission Viejo. The City will have its own Prelude in the Park and Symphony in the Cities
event on the Village Green on Saturday July 27, 2019. Council Member Bucknum noted that the
City will also host two more concerts on the Village Green and Camp Out Under the Stars in
August. Although the camping event is sold out, residents can get on a waiting list. She also
announced Montanoso Recreation Center has a pool inflatable for residents to enjoy on Sunday
afternoons in the summer.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley thanked the dedicated volunteers of the Mission Viejo Activities
Committee who put on the 4th of July Street Faire each year. She, along with Council Member
Bucknum, attended last week and she said it’s a wonderful celebration put on by a small number
of people, but it benefits thousands. Council Member Kelley thanked Commissioner Pam Smith
and the Activities Committee for planning the event. She discussed her attendance at the Senior
Corps of Retirees (SCOR) appreciation event where Sheriff’s Department volunteers were
recognized for providing services such as vacation home checks, neighborhood patrols,
volunteering at the front desk, and a variety of other things. She said she appreciated the
opportunity to attend the event and personally thank those volunteers for providing a service that
saves the City a lot of money. Council Member Kelley announced that on Sunday, July 21, the
Mission Viejo Marine Adoption Committee will host Boots, Beer and BBQ to benefit the City’s
adopted Headquarters Battalion from Camp Pendleton. The event is from 4:00 to 7:00 p.m. at the
Murray Community Center and tickets can be purchased ahead of time for $25 per person either
online or at the Community Center. Council Member Kelley recapped the Mission Viejo
Community of Character program and noted that the character quality for the month of July is
fairness. In closing, she shared a quote by Michael Josephson: “A person of character plays fair
even when others don’t and values no achievement unless it was attained with honor.”

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs highlighted the profile of Mission Viejo in the new Southern California
Association of Governments (SCAG) publication. He pointed out the extraordinary data in the
profile which includes information that 21-34-year-olds are growing in the City as well as 35-54-
year-olds. He expressed concern that the report shows that retail sales boomed in 2005 and have
steadily gone down since then. Council Member Sachs noted that retail sales were $18 per person
in 2005 and have since gone below $14. He stressed that some of the main issues the City Council
has to address are related to the downturn in revenues.

City Council Minutes  7  July 9, 2019
 Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell spoke about the due diligence that will be taking place over the summer
hiatus for the golf course and said he looks forward to working with staff and the developer. He
announced that the Masters National Championship Swim Meet will take place in Mission Viejo
August 7-11 and he will be swimming in the event. He also mentioned that the Masters Diving
Championship will take place later this month.

Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths announced that Mission Viejo has received a “Gigabit City” award from Cox
Communications and he discussed his attendance at the ribbon cutting ceremony for the newly
remodeled Gateway Center. He also thanked the vendors and the Mission Viejo Activities
Committee for a wonderful 4th of July Street Faire. Mayor Raths announced that the City and
Rotary Club will host a Big Splash Belly Flop Contest on August 2, 2019, at 6:00 p.m. at Sierra
Recreation Center.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:28 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, August 27, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, Asssistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of August 27, 2019

City Council Minutes  8  July 9, 2019
